main_system_reason: The castle is the only part of Dholavira whose fortification and inner walls are conserved and clearly visible over long stretches; sys1 joins its north and south walls, the E-W walls inside it and the inner face of its east wall, which agree within a few degrees. The bailey wall (sys2) runs in the same direction. The middle and lower towns are overgrown, so the castle is the best available witness of the town's layout.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic built from a WorldView-2 scene of 18 December 2023, with real detail to zoom 18 (0.55 m per pixel). The low December sun casts long shadows to the north-west, so the north faces of E-W walls and the west faces of N-S walls show as sharp dark lines, and we measured on those lines. The castle walls are conserved with new masonry on the Harappan courses. Its north and south walls and the E-W walls inside it run several degrees counterclockwise of east, and the inner face of the east wall, which we measured along the deep trench that exposes it, runs counterclockwise of north by a smaller angle, so the castle is not a perfect rectangle in this reading. DC3, a N-S line in the western part of the castle, is made of two aligned wall segments that may belong to different buildings; it differs from the castle walls by several degrees, and we report it as its own low-confidence system. The bailey west of the castle is mostly overgrown; one wall of 35 m is exposed in its north-east. North of the castle a long pale E-W band and several N-S bands cross the middle and lower town; they are excavated strips that expose walls in places, but their edges are excavation cuts and visitor paths and the walls inside them do not stay continuous, so we did not measure them. The great reservoirs, the stadium-like open ground and the outer fortification are not resolved as straight wall lines on this image.
